citation: Kovaleva V, Yu LY, Ivanova L, et al. MANF regulates neuronal survival and UPR through its ER-located receptor IRE1alpha. Cell Reports. 2023;42:112066.
description: This paper shows that MANF directly binds the ER UPR sensor IRE1alpha and that wild-type MANF suppresses IRE1alpha phosphorylation, Xbp1 splicing, Atf6 and Txnip levels, and ER-stress-induced neuronal death. It supports the expectation that MANF loss can release unfolded-protein-response signaling.

citation: Yu Y, Liu DY, Chen XS, Zhu L, Wan LH. MANF: A Novel Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response Protein-The Role in Neurological and Metabolic Disorders. Oxidative Medicine and Cellular Longevity. 2021;6467679.
description: This review summarizes MANF as a conserved ER-stress-response and UPR-related protein with protective activity in neurological and metabolic contexts. It supports interpreting Hspa5, Hyou1, Dnajb9, and Pdia6 induction as an ER-stress response to Manf perturbation.

citation: Pressey JC, de Saint-Rome M, Raveendran VA, Woodin MA. Chloride transporters controlling neuronal excitability. Physiological Reviews. 2022;102.
description: This review documents that KCC2 is the main neuronal chloride extruder and that KCC2 hypofunction shifts GABA/glycine signaling by disrupting chloride-dependent inhibition. It provides the target-specific bridge from Slc12a5 loss to altered excitability.

citation: Hu JJ, Liu Y, Yao H, et al. Emergence of consciousness from anesthesia through ubiquitin degradation of KCC2 in the ventral posteromedial nucleus of the thalamus. Nature Neuroscience. 2023;26.
description: This mouse study shows that rapid KCC2 downregulation in the ventral posteromedial thalamus causes GABA-A-receptor-mediated disinhibition and increased VPM neuron excitability. It supports the Slc12a5-to-excitability bridge in a thalamic glutamatergic context.

citation: Goncalves V, Jordan P. Posttranscriptional Regulation of Splicing Factor SRSF1 and Its Role in Cancer Cell Biology. BioMed Research International. 2015;287048.
description: This review describes SRSF1 as a prototypical splicing regulator whose localization, phosphorylation, and alternative splicing control RNA isoform production. It supports using an RNA-processing bridge for Srsf1-centered splicing-factor responses without establishing exact target-gene directions.

citation: Zhou Y, Liu S, Liu G, Ozturk A, Hicks GG. ALS-associated FUS mutations result in compromised FUS alternative splicing and autoregulation. PLoS Genetics. 2013;9:e1003895.
description: This study used FUS CLIP-seq and perturbation to show that FUS binds pre-mRNA and regulates alternative splicing, including autoregulation through exon 7. It supports a specific RNA-processing bridge for Fus perturbations.

citation: Bain JM, Cho MT, Telegrafi A, et al. Variants in HNRNPH2 on the X Chromosome Are Associated with a Neurodevelopmental Disorder in Females. American Journal of Human Genetics. 2016;99:728-734.
description: This paper identifies HNRNPH2 variants in a neurodevelopmental syndrome and notes that HNRNP proteins associate with pre-mRNAs to regulate alternative splicing. It provides a target-specific but incomplete bridge between Hnrnph2 perturbation and RNA-processing responses.

citation: Tan ZW, Fei G, Paulo JA, et al. O-GlcNAc regulates gene expression by controlling detained intron splicing. Nucleic Acids Research. 2020;48:5656-5669.
description: This study shows that O-GlcNAc cycling regulates detained-intron splicing of OGT, OGA, and many transcripts, coupling OGT activity to transcript abundance. It supports a specific Ogt-to-RNA-processing bridge while leaving the assayed neuronal target genes unresolved.

citation: Maertens GN, Cook NJ, Wang W, et al. Structural basis for nuclear import of splicing factors by human Transportin 3. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2014;111:2728-2733.
description: This work shows that TNPO3 binds phosphorylated RS domains and mediates nuclear import of the SR splicing factor ASF/SF2. It gives a specific bridge from Tnpo3 perturbation to SR/splicing-factor biology but not to the measured expression directions.

citation: Ebrahimi-Fakhari D, Saffari A, Wahlster L, et al. Impaired Mitochondrial Dynamics and Mitophagy in Neuronal Models of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. Cell Reports. 2016;17:2162-2175.
description: This paper shows that Tsc1/2-deficient neurons activate mTORC1, accumulate mitochondria, and have impaired global and axonal mitophagy that can be restored by mTORC1 blockade or mTOR-independent autophagy induction. It supports an indirect bridge from Tsc1 loss to autophagy and mitochondrial pathway changes.

citation: Muona M, Ishimura R, Laari A, et al. Biallelic Variants in UBA5 Link Dysfunctional UFM1 Ubiquitin-like Modifier Pathway to Severe Infantile-Onset Encephalopathy. American Journal of Human Genetics. 2016;99:683-694.
description: This paper links loss-of-function UBA5 alleles to early infantile encephalopathy and shows that CNS-specific Ufm1 knockout in mice causes microcephaly and neuronal apoptosis. It supports the relevance of UBA5/UFM1 activity to the nervous system without predicting the exact acute transcriptomic module.

citation: Lipiec MA, Bem J, Kozinski K, et al. TCF7L2 regulates postmitotic differentiation programmes and excitability patterns in the thalamus. Development. 2020;147:dev190181.
description: This mouse knockout study shows that Tcf7l2 controls postmitotic thalamic differentiation and induction of terminal electrophysiological features. It supports a thalamic identity/excitability bridge for the Tcf7l2 thalamic response.

citation: Lee M, Yoon J, Song H, et al. Tcf7l2 plays crucial roles in forebrain development through regulation of thalamic and habenular neuron identity and connectivity. Developmental Biology. 2017;424:62-76.
description: This developmental mouse study shows that Tcf7l2 loss disrupts thalamocortical axon guidance and causes postmitotic identity switching between thalamic and habenular neurons. It supplies cell-type identity support for Tcf7l2 but from an embryonic germline context.

citation: Mangieri LR, Mader BJ, Thomas CE, et al. ATP6V0C knockdown in neuroblastoma cells alters autophagy-lysosome pathway function and metabolism of proteins that accumulate in neurodegenerative disease. PLoS One. 2014;9:e93257.
description: This study establishes ATP6V0C as a V-ATPase subunit required for lysosomal acidification and autophagy-lysosome pathway flux in neuronally differentiated SH-SY5Y cells. It supports a V-ATPase/autophagy bridge for Atp6v0c responses.

citation: Chung CY, Shin HR, Berdan CA, et al. Covalent targeting of the vacuolar H+-ATPase activates autophagy via mTORC1 inhibition. Nature Chemical Biology. 2019;15:776-785.
description: This chemical-biology study shows that covalent targeting of ATP6V1A decouples lysosomal V-ATPase from Rag GTPases, inhibits mTORC1 signaling, and activates autophagy. It gives a V-ATPase/mTOR/autophagy bridge for Atp6v1a perturbation.

citation: Wang L, Xu Y, Rogers H, et al. UFMylation of RPL26 links translocation-associated quality control to endoplasmic reticulum protein homeostasis. Cell Research. 2019;30:5-20.
description: This work shows that UFM1 conjugation on RPL26 supports quality control for ER-translocation-stalled nascent chains, and that compromised UFMylation impairs secretion and is tied to abnormal neuronal development. It supports an indirect ER-quality-control bridge for Uba5 loss.

citation: Wisner SR, Chlebowski M, Mandal A, et al. An initial HOPS-mediated fusion event is critical for autophagosome transport initiation from the axon terminal. Autophagy. 2024;20.
description: Using zebrafish vps18 and vps41 loss-of-function mutants, this study shows that HOPS-mediated fusion is required for autophagosome maturation and retrograde autophagosome transport from axon terminals. It supports a specific neuronal autophagy bridge for Vps41.
